abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achbor-2.title: Achbor
achbor-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
achbor-2.note: A different Achbor entirely, from the time of the patriarchs. Genesis names him only as somebody's father.

adah.title: Adah
adah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
adah.note: One of Esau's wives. She is named through the family lists in Genesis and not outside them.

adullamite.title: Adullamite
adullamite.note: Hirah, Judah's friend in the story of Judah and Tamar, was one. It means a man from Adullam, a Canaanite town in Judah's territory.

aholibamah.title: Aholibamah
aholibamah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
aholibamah.note: She was one of Esau's wives, the daughter of a Hivite chief, and her sons became tribal leaders among the Edomites.

aiah-2.title: Aiah
aiah-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aiah-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

akan.title: Akan
akan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
akan.note: He was Ezer's son and one of the Horite clan chiefs descended from Seir, in the land of Edom before Israel had a king. 1 Chronicles 1:42 spells him Jakan.

aliah.title: Aliah
aliah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aliah.note: Another spelling of Alvah, one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau. The two Edomite lists in Genesis and Chronicles differ in small ways like this throughout, and nothing further is recorded of him.

alian.title: Alian
alian.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
alian.note: Also called Alvan. He was a son of Shobal and a Horite clan chief in Seir, and nothing further is known.

allon-bachuth.title: Allon-bachuth
allon-bachuth.note: Oak of weeping. It is the place near Bethel where Rebekah's nurse Deborah was buried, and it was likely the same landmark later called the palm tree of Deborah, where the judge Deborah held court.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

amalek-2.title: Amalek
amalek-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
amalek-2.note: Genesis names him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

anah.title: Anah
anah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
anah.note: He found hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father's donkeys, and he sits in the Edomite genealogies of Esau's line.

aran.title: Aran
aran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aran.note: A descendant of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs of Edom. The Horites were the cave-dwelling people of Mount Seir before the Edomites pushed them out, and lists like this keep their tribal structure. Nothing else about him is recorded.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

avith.title: Avith
avith.note: The city of Hadad son of Bedad, one of the early kings of Edom before Israel had kings of its own. He beat the Midianites in the territory of Moab.

baal-hanan.title: Baal-hanan
baal-hanan.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
baal-hanan.note: An Edomite king, from the list in Genesis of rulers who reigned before Israel had a king of its own.

bashemath.title: Bashemath
bashemath.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bashemath.note: One of Esau's wives, in the Genesis lists. The name belongs to more than one of them, and to a daughter of Solomon too.

bashemath-2.title: Bashemath
bashemath-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bashemath-2.note: Another of Esau's wives with this name, the one in the Genesis 36 lists.

bedad.title: Bedad
bedad.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
bedad.note: Hadad's father. Hadad was one of the early kings of Edom, and he beat the Midianites in the territory of Moab. Nothing else is recorded of Bedad.

bela-2.title: Bela
bela-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
bela-2.note: An early king, first on the Genesis 36 list, from long before Israel had a throne.

ben-oni.title: Ben-oni
ben-oni.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ben-oni.note: Son of my sorrow. Rachel gave the name to her second son as she was dying in childbirth near Bethlehem. Jacob renamed the boy Benjamin, son of the right hand.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beor-2.title: Beor
beor-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
beor-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bilhah.title: Bilhah
bilhah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bilhah.note: Rachel's maidservant. Laban had given her to Rachel, and when Rachel had no children she gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife. Bilhah bore him Dan and Naphtali.

bilhan.title: Bilhan
bilhan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
bilhan.note: A Horite clan chief, in Edom's genealogies.

bozrah.title: Bozrah
bozrah.note: Edom's capital, the city of the early Edomite king Jobab. The prophets kept coming back to it in their oracles against Edom. Isaiah pictures the Lord coming from Bozrah in stained garments.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

cheran.title: Cheran
cheran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
cheran.note: Dishon's son, from the Horite clans of Seir. The Horites lived in the region before Edom's kings arose and were later pushed out or absorbed.

chezib.title: Chezib
chezib.note: The town where Shelah, Judah's third son by his Canaanite wife, was born, generally taken as another name for Achzib in the Shephelah, though nobody has found the site.

dan-2.title: Dan
dan-2.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
dan-2.note: Jacob's son by Bilhah, Rachel's servant, and the ancestor of the tribe that carries his name.

deborah-2.title: Deborah
deborah-2.about: Nurse living at the time of the Patriarchs
deborah-2.note: Rebekah's nurse, who went with her from Haran and stayed with the family for life. Genesis 35:8 records her death and burial under an oak below Bethel, which was named the oak of weeping.

dinah.title: Dinah
dinah.about: Jacob's daughter living at the time of the Patriarchs
dinah.note: Jacob and Leah's only daughter. After Shechem raped her, Simeon and Levi made the men of his city agree to be circumcised and then killed them all while they were still recovering. On his deathbed Jacob condemned it as reckless cruelty.

dinhaban.title: Dinhaban
dinhaban.note: A place, not a person, and a variant spelling of Dinhabah, the capital of Bela son of Beor, first on Edom's list of early kings. It lay somewhere south and east of the Dead Sea; the site is unknown.

dishan.title: Dishan
dishan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishan.note: Youngest of the sons of Seir, a Horite chief among Edom's earlier people.

dishon.title: Dishon
dishon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishon.note: One of the Horite chiefs who held Edom's land before Esau's descendants settled it.

dishon-2.title: Dishon
dishon-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishon-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

ebal.title: Ebal
ebal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ebal.note: The mountain of the curses, opposite Mount Gerizim near Shechem. Moses ordered six tribes onto Ebal to speak the covenant's curses while six on Gerizim spoke its blessings, and Joshua built an altar there and wrote the law on stones. A Horite chief descended from Seir carried the name too.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elah-3.title: Elah
elah-3.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
elah-3.note: One of 5 men called Elah. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

eliphaz.title: Eliphaz
eliphaz.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
eliphaz.note: Esau's son, the first of the Edomite line in Genesis 36, and father of a string of Edomite chiefs.

elon.title: Elon
elon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
elon.note: A Hittite whose daughter Basemath married Esau; the name means oak.

enaim.title: Enaim
enaim.note: Tamar sat veiled at Enaim and waited for Judah, who had not given her his youngest son. The name means two springs, or two eyes, and the spot is usually placed between Adullam and Timnah.

er.title: Er
er.note: Judah's firstborn. Genesis says only that he was wicked in the Lord's sight and God put him to death, and his widow Tamar's story starts from there.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

esau-2.title: Esau
esau-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau-2.note: A man from the patriarchs. Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him 7 times.

eshban.title: Eshban
eshban.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
eshban.note: One of Dishon's four sons, a Horite among the clan chiefs of Seir.

ezer.title: Ezer
ezer.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ezer.note: A chieftain of Seir, named in Edom's early lists of clan heads.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

galeed.title: Galeed
galeed.note: Not a person but a heap of stones. Jacob and Laban piled it up to seal their covenant. Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha in Aramaic, and Jacob's Hebrew name for it means heap of witness.

gatam.title: Gatam
gatam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
gatam.note: Esau's grandson through Eliphaz, and one of the chiefs of Edom, the dukes of the old translations, heading a clan and otherwise only a name in the lists.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

hadad-2.title: Hadad
hadad-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadad-2.note: One of the kings of Edom, in Genesis 36 and the matching list in Chronicles. The name was common among them.

hadar.title: Hadar
hadar.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadar.note: The last of the Edomite kings listed before Israel had a king. He ruled from Pau and his wife was Mehetabel. Chronicles calls him Hadad, so Hadar may only be a copying variant.

hamor.title: Hamor
hamor.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hamor.note: The Canaanite ruler of Shechem. His son raped Dinah, and while Hamor tried to arrange a marriage, Simeon and Levi talked the men of the city into circumcision and killed them while they were still in pain.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hemam.title: Hemam
hemam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hemam.note: Lotan's son and grandson of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs, and 1 Chronicles 1:39 calls him Homam.

hemdan.title: Hemdan
hemdan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hemdan.note: Eldest son of Dishon, one of the Horite chiefs who held the land before Esau's descendants took it. Chronicles calls him Hamran.

hirah.title: Hirah
hirah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hirah.note: Judah's friend from Adullam. He was there when Judah married a Canaanite woman. Later Judah sent him with a goat to pay the woman he had slept with, who was Tamar in disguise.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hori.title: Hori
hori.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hori.note: In Edom's genealogies he is one of the Horite clan chiefs, and that is all the record gives.

horims.title: Horims
horims.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
horims.note: They lived in the region that became Edom before Esau's descendants pushed them out. Genesis records them as the land's earlier people.

husham.title: Husham
husham.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
husham.note: He was king of Edom in the days before Israel had any king.

iram.title: Iram
iram.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
iram.note: A clan chief of Edom, from Esau's descendants in the hill country of Seir.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

ishmael-2.title: Ishmael
ishmael-2.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmael-2.note: Abraham's first son, by Hagar, Sarah's servant. Sarah had given Hagar to Abraham while she was still childless, then wanted mother and son gone after Isaac came. God promised Hagar her son would father a great nation too, though the covenant line ran through Isaac.

ishmaelite.title: Ishmaelite
ishmaelite.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmaelite.note: The Ishmaelites came from Abraham's son Ishmael and traded across the country south and east of Canaan. One of their caravans bought Joseph from his brothers and took him down to Egypt.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

ithran.title: Ithran
ithran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ithran.note: A Horite clan name, from Edom's earlier inhabitants.

jabbok.title: Jabbok
jabbok.note: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jalam.title: Jalam
jalam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jalam.note: Esau's son by Oholibamah, whose descendants became one of Edom's clans.

jegar-sahadutha.title: Jegar-Sahadutha
jegar-sahadutha.note: Laban's Aramaic name for the heap of stones he and Jacob raised in Gilead to witness their covenant. Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean "heap of witness".

jehush.title: Jehush
jehush.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jehush.note: Esau's son, more often spelled Jeush. Several other men in Chronicles carry the name.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

jobab.title: Jobab
jobab.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
jobab.note: An early king of Edom, from the list in Genesis 36 of kings who ruled there before Israel had any.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kenaz.title: Kenaz
kenaz.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
kenaz.note: One of Edom's clan chiefs, in Genesis 36 and again in Chronicles. The Kenizzites are counted among the Edomite clans.

kirjath-arba.title: Kirjath-arba
kirjath-arba.note: "Arba's city," Hebron's older name, after a great man among the Anakim. Sarah died there and Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah close by to bury her. Joshua gave it to Caleb for the faithful report he brought back as a spy.

korah-2.title: Korah
korah-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
korah-2.note: An Edomite chief in Genesis 36 and Chronicles, with nothing to do with the Levite who rebelled.

korah-4.title: Korah
korah-4.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
korah-4.note: One of 4 men called Korah. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named once in Genesis.

laban.title: Laban
laban.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
laban.note: Rebekah's brother and Jacob's uncle, and then his father-in-law twice, after he slipped Leah in where Rachel should have been and got fourteen years of work out of him. He kept changing Jacob's wages as the flocks grew. Jacob finally slipped away with his family, and the two parted under a covenant, not with a fight.

leah.title: Leah
leah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
leah.note: Jacob's first wife, given to him by her father Laban in place of Rachel, and Jacob only found out in the morning. He never loved her the way he loved Rachel. Genesis says God gave her children because she was unloved, and she bore six of the twelve sons, Judah among them.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

lotan.title: Lotan
lotan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
lotan.note: He was a Horite chief whose sister Timna made him Esau's brother-in-law, and his people were living in Edom's land before Edom.

magdiel.title: Magdiel
magdiel.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
magdiel.note: One of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, in the lists at Genesis 36:43 and 1 Chronicles 1:54. The name may mark a clan territory more than a single ruler.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

mamre.title: Mamre
mamre.note: Near Hebron, where Abraham settled and built an altar. The three visitors who told him Isaac was coming found him there. Mamre was also the name of an Amorite who stood with Abraham as an ally.

manahath.title: Manahath
manahath.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
manahath.note: Shobal's son, Seir the Horite's grandson, and a clan chief of Edom in Genesis and Chronicles. The same name shows up in Benjamin's genealogy, probably for the related Manahathites, who are tied elsewhere to Zorah and Caleb's family.

masrekah.title: Masrekah
masrekah.note: Samlah came from this town in Edom. He was one of the kings who ruled there before Israel had a king of its own.

matred.title: Matred
matred.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
matred.note: Mezahab's daughter, and the mother of Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list. Women are rare in those lists, and nothing more is said of her.

mehetabeel.title: Mehetabeel
mehetabeel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
mehetabeel.note: Wife of one of the early kings of Edom, in the king lists of Genesis and Chronicles.

mezahab.title: Mezahab
mezahab.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mezahab.note: Matred's father. His great claim is a granddaughter, Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list.

mibzar.title: Mibzar
mibzar.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mibzar.note: "Fortress." One of the chiefs of Edom from Esau's line, and like several names in that list it probably stands for a clan territory or stronghold as much as a man.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

migdal-eder.title: Migdal-eder
migdal-eder.note: "Tower of the flock," near Bethlehem. Jacob pitched his tent there after burying Rachel by the road. Micah uses the name for Jerusalem's stronghold, promising its old rule would come back to the daughter of Zion.

mizzah.title: Mizzah
mizzah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mizzah.note: A clan chief of Edom, from Esau's line, and the record has no more.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

nahath.title: Nahath
nahath.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahath.note: An Edomite chief from Esau's line. The name was also carried by a Levite in Chronicles.

nahor.title: Nahor
nahor.about: Abraham's brother living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahor.note: Abraham's brother, Terah's son, who stayed in Mesopotamia when Abraham went to Canaan. His family there gave Isaac a wife, Rebekah, and gave Jacob his uncle and father-in-law, Laban.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebaioth.title: Nebaioth
nebaioth.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
nebaioth.note: Ishmael's firstborn. His descendants were an Arabian trading people, named next to Kedar in Isaiah.

omar.title: Omar
omar.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
omar.note: Esau's grandson and an Edomite clan chief, listed in the genealogies of Genesis 36.

onam-2.title: Onam
onam-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
onam-2.note: A Horite clan name in Edom's genealogies, listed in Genesis 36:23 and again in 1 Chronicles 1:40.

onan.title: Onan
onan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
onan.note: Judah's second son. Custom required him to father a child for his dead brother through the widow Tamar. He made sure it never happened, and God put him to death for it.

padan.title: Padan
padan.note: Short for Paddan-aram, the country around Haran in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's brother Nahor settled. Rebekah came from there. Jacob ran there years later to get away from Esau.

pai.title: Pai
pai.note: Hadar, last of Edom's early kings in the Genesis list, ruled from Pai, also spelled Pau, and nobody knows where in Edom it stood.

peniel.title: Peniel
peniel.note: Jacob wrestled here through the night by the Jabbok River. He came away with a new name, Israel, and a limp he kept. He called the place Peniel, face of God, because he had seen God face to face and lived.

perez.title: Perez
perez.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
perez.note: Judah's son by Tamar. He pushed out ahead of his twin Zerah, though Zerah's hand had already been marked with a scarlet thread as the firstborn. His line runs through Boaz to David.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pharaoh-2.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-2.note: Joseph's Pharaoh. Potiphar was his officer, his baker and butler landed in prison with Joseph, and his dreams of fat and thin cows were what got Joseph out and set him over Egypt.

pinon.title: Pinon
pinon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
pinon.note: An Edomite chief in Genesis 36:41 and 1 Chronicles 1:52, whom many scholars take to be the same name as Punon.

potiphar.title: Potiphar
potiphar.about: Egyptian living at the time of the Patriarchs
potiphar.note: An Egyptian official. He bought Joseph as a slave and soon had him running the whole household. When Potiphar's wife accused Joseph falsely, Potiphar had him put in prison.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

raguel.title: Raguel
raguel.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
raguel.note: In Genesis 36 he is an Edomite chief. The record elsewhere ties the name to Jethro, Moses's father-in-law, the Midianite priest, but these verses are the Edomite.

rebekah.title: Rebekah
rebekah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rebekah.note: Abraham's servant went back to Mesopotamia to find Isaac a wife. He asked for water, and Rebekah offered to water his camels too. That was the sign he had been waiting for.

rehoboth.title: Rehoboth
rehoboth.note: It means broad places, and the name turns up in more than one spot. Genesis 10:11 puts a Rehoboth among the cities built in Assyria, and an Edomite king came from a Rehoboth by the river.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

samlah.title: Samlah
samlah.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
samlah.note: Edom had kings before Israel did, and Samlah was one of them.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

seir-2.title: Seir
seir-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
seir-2.note: Seir the Horite, whose sons are listed in Genesis 36:20 and again in 1 Chronicles 1:38. They were the people in the land before Esau's line took it.

shammah.title: Shammah
shammah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shammah.note: Genesis 36 has a Shammah among its chiefs, and 1 Samuel 16:9 and 17:13 name one as a brother of David. The name was used more than once.

shaul.title: Shaul
shaul.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
shaul.note: A king from the patriarchs. Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him 4 times.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shechem-2.title: Shechem
shechem-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shechem-2.note: The Canaanite prince who raped Jacob's daughter Dinah. Her brothers Simeon and Levi answered it with a massacre.

shelah.title: Shelah
shelah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shelah.note: Judah's third son by his Canaanite wife. Judah held him back from marrying Tamar, the widow, as custom said he should. That broken promise is what drove Tamar to disguise herself.

shephi.title: Shephi
shephi.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
shephi.note: Son of Shobal, of the line of Seir the Horite, among Edom's clan chiefs, and Genesis 36:23 spells him Shepho.

shobal.title: Shobal
shobal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
shobal.note: An Edomite clan chief, descended from Seir. The name was used again for a man of Judah.

shua.title: Shua
shua.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shua.note: A Canaanite. Judah married his daughter, and she bore Er, Onan and Shelah.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

syrian-2.title: Syrian
syrian-2.note: In Genesis the word marks the family in Paddan-aram as Arameans, and Deuteronomy 26:5 uses it once more.

tamar-2.title: Tamar
tamar-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
tamar-2.note: Judah's daughter-in-law, widowed twice with no heir. Judah held back his third son, so she dressed as a prostitute and conceived twins by Judah himself. He ended up saying she was more righteous than he was, and Ruth 4:12 blesses a family in her name.

temani.title: Temani
temani.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
temani.note: Teman was Esau's grandson, and his Edomite clan had a name for wisdom. This is the word for that clan, and it is what Eliphaz is called all through Job.

timna.title: Timna
timna.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
timna.note: Two Edomites. One was a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, and her son Amalek fathered the people who were Israel's enemies for generations. The other was an Edomite clan chief.

uz-3.title: Uz
uz-3.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
uz-3.note: One of 4 men called Uz. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

zaavan.title: Zaavan
zaavan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zaavan.note: An Edomite chief descended from Seir the Horite, also spelled Zavan.

zarah.title: Zarah
zarah.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarah.note: Judah's son by Tamar, Perez's twin. His hand came out first and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, and then Perez was born ahead of him.

zarah-4.title: Zarah
zarah-4.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
zarah-4.note: One of 6 men called Zarah. This one is a king from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

zarah-2.title: Zarah
zarah-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zarah-2.note: Not Judah's son. This Zerah is in the Genesis 36 family lists and in 1 Chronicles 1:37, one of the Idumaean names.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zephi.title: Zephi
zephi.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zephi.note: Eliphaz's son and Esau's grandson, one of the clan chiefs of Edom. Nothing more is recorded.

zibeon.title: Zibeon
zibeon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zibeon.note: A Horite chief in the Edom lists of Genesis 36, and Esau's wife Oholibamah came from his line.

zilpah.title: Zilpah
zilpah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
zilpah.note: Leah's servant. In the contest between Leah and Rachel for sons she was given to Jacob, and she bore him Gad and Asher.
